editorial.headline: The Retail Business Where Art, Music and Collecting Meet
editorial.standfirst: This activity brings together specialist retail in art, music, recorded media and collecting—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is a specialist retail home for the cultural and recreational objects that invite attention rather than impulse. It covers the sale of recorded media; musical instruments, sheet music and related accessories such as strings, music stands and metronomes; and collectible material including stamps and coins. It also includes commercial art galleries, alongside the retail of art supplies—from beads and clay to canvas, oil paints and watercolours. The common thread is not one product category but a retail practice built around making, listening, collecting and exhibiting.

That breadth gives the activity a recognisable commercial shape. A business may trade in the practical tools of artistic work, the equipment and scores that support musical practice, or objects whose value lies in rarity, cultural interest or collection. A commercial gallery belongs within the same activity, placing the sale and presentation of art alongside more conventional specialist retail. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved for one size of operator.

Nationally, the position is direct: the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That national opening is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But Bali requires a separate reading. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk; Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. The Bali status is therefore BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, reflecting a provincial barrier that sits alongside—not beneath—the national openness.

For founders, the important distinction is between the activity’s national investment position and its current registrability in Bali. Full foreign ownership is available nationally, yet that does not create a route for PMA registration on the island where the permanent moratorium applies. The business itself remains clearly defined: specialist retail for recorded media, music, collecting, art materials and commercial gallery activity. The constraint is geographical and regulatory, not a narrowing of that underlying scope.
